explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is a full-stack, self-hosted web-based file manager (“FileBrowser Quantum”).  
   - It provides a Vue.js single-page application (SPA) frontend, a Go-based REST API backend, file storage adapters, a BoltDB database, real-time indexing and preview services, pluggable authentication (OIDC, TOTP, proxy), and a CLI.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top-level “frontend/”: contains a Vite/Vue 3 SPA with components, router, store, assets, CSS, API client modules, and Playwright end-to-end tests.  
   - Top-level “backend/”: a Go module with subpackages for HTTP (router, middleware, Swagger), authentication, adapters (FS, cache), database (Bolt), indexing, preview engines, events, settings, and CLI commands.  
   - “_docker/”: Dockerfiles and compose configurations for different runtime modes (general, noauth, proxy) and for running Playwright tests.  
   - Configuration files: YAML for both backend and Docker.  
   - Test suites: Go unit tests, JavaScript unit tests, and Playwright E2E.

3. Extract additional insights from README  
   - Tech stack: Vue 3 + Vite + Playwright; Go 1.x; BoltDB; Docker.  
   - Architectural highlights: modular monolith in Go with clear adapter boundaries, real-time indexing, preview pipeline, Swagger API docs, multiple deployment modes.

4. How to draw the system design diagram  
   a. Main components  
      • Browser (Client)  
      • Frontend SPA (Vue.js, Vite)  
      • Backend API Server (Go HTTP server)  
      • Authentication Module (OIDC provider, proxy handler, JSON/TOTP)  
      • File System Adapters (diskcache, file operations)  
      • Database (BoltDB storage)  
      • Indexing Service (file watcher + real-time search index)  
      • Preview Service (image, office, video previews)  
      • Swagger UI (auto-generated API docs)  
      • CLI (admin commands via same Go modules)  
      • External Services (OIDC IdP, OnlyOffice integration)  
      • Docker Containers/Compose (frontend container, backend container, test containers)  

   b. Relationships and interactions  
      1. Browser ↔ Frontend SPA  
      2. SPA → Backend API (HTTP/HTTPS) → JSON responses, file streams, previews  
      3. Backend → BoltDB for user, settings, share, index metadata  
      4. Backend → File storage (local FS or configured mount) via adapters  
      5. Indexing Service watches FS changes, updates the index store, notifies backend events  
      6. Preview Service invoked by backend on demand for generating thumbnails/previews  
      7. Auth Module intercepts API calls, validates via DB, OIDC provider, TOTP or proxy headers  
      8. CLI commands invoke backend modules directly for batch operations (user mgmt, shares)  
      9. Swagger UI served at `/swagger`, backed by auto-generated docs  
      10. Optional external OnlyOffice service connected via HTTP for office editing  

   c. Architectural patterns and design principles  
      • Modular monolith with clearly defined adapter interfaces (storage, auth).  
      • Layered approach: HTTP layer → business logic (auth, indexing, preview) → persistence.  
      • Event-driven indexing and notification.  
      • Configuration-driven deployment modes (general, noauth, proxy).  
      • Shared code between HTTP handlers and CLI.  

   d. Key technologies and frameworks  
      • Frontend: Vue.js 3, Vite, Vue Router, Vuex/Pinia (store), Playwright  
      • Backend: Go, Gorilla-style HTTP router, BoltDB, YAML configs, Go modules  
      • Build & Deployment: Docker, Docker Compose, Makefile, GitHub Actions workflows  
      • API docs: Swagger (OpenAPI) auto-generated  

5. Tailoring the diagram for this full-stack application  
   - Draw three primary tiers:  
     1. Presentation Tier: Browser → Vue SPA  
     2. Application Tier: Go API Server (with submodules for auth, indexing, preview)  
     3. Data Tier: BoltDB, File System storage  
   - Include optional external entities: OIDC identity provider, OnlyOffice server.  
   - Show different Docker container roles: SPA container, API container, test container.  

6. Diagramming guidelines  
   - Label each component clearly (e.g., “Vue SPA”, “Go HTTP API”).  
   - Use directional arrows to indicate data flow:  
     • User actions → SPA → API → Storage → SPA → Browser  
   - Color-code shapes by type:  
     • Blue for frontend/UI,  
     • Green for backend/services,  
     • Orange for storage/databases,  
     • Purple for external services.  
   - Use different shapes: rectangles for services, cylinders for databases, clouds for external services.  
   - Annotate each arrow with the protocol or data type (e.g., HTTP/JSON, WebSocket events, file streams).  

7. Emphasis on detail  
   - Don’t just draw one big “backend” box—break it into Auth, API Router, Indexing, Preview, CLI.  
   - Show the FS adapter layer between API logic and the underlying file share.  
   - Illustrate the real-time indexing loop: watcher → index store → API event router → SPA via HTTP events or polling.  
   - Capture multiple deployment modes by annotating runtime flags or separate container images (general vs. noauth vs. proxy).  
   - Include a legend explaining color-coding and shapes.

By following these steps and including the elements above, you’ll produce a system design diagram that fully represents FileBrowser Quantum’s architecture, clarifies component interactions, and highlights the technology stack.  
</explanation>
